subject: physical-education

location.unitTitle: Safety, Self-Care, and Knowing When to Stop
location.courseTitle: Lifelong Wellness and Independent Training Capstone

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the safe activity or accessible equivalent and document the requested performance evidence.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing trouble, unsafe conditions, or missing adult supervision.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of the stop rule as an adult habit rather than a class instruction in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe distinguishing training discomfort from warning pain using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply illness, injury, and graded return without a coach in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving sleep, fuel, and recovery as the base of any plan; correct it and explain why.
Connect when to see a clinician and how to describe a problem with building self-care into a plan instead of bolting it on and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Write the self-care and stop-rule protocol the learner will actually run as an adult, including the specific conditions under which they will stop, rest, or seek professional care.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated safe participation and self-management criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated skill cues or movement quality criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated tactical or training reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated self-assessment and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Safety, Self-Care, and Knowing When to Stop?
